Rugged tablets for field service engineers

Job sheets, manuals, photos and a customer signature at the end. A field service tablet spends its life between the van and the plant room, and it should be built for both.

What we'd buy

Tuga A8

The all-rounder. Fits the van door pocket.

8″ / IP67 / 8000mAh removable

£379 Full spec

Field service work is driving, diagnosing and documenting. The job comes in on the tablet, the manual is on it, and the customer signs on it before you leave.

What kills devices in field service

  • Plant rooms and boiler cupboards. Heat, oil, grease and the occasional leak. A device put down on top of a unit or on a wet floor gets whatever is there.
  • Van life. Hours on a dashboard in summer sun, a cold start on a winter morning, and being thrown on the passenger seat between jobs.
  • Flat batteries at the wrong moment. The last job of the day is when the customer wants to sign and the tablet is on 3%.
  • Drops. Off a ladder, off a roof hatch, out of the van door. The usual.
  • Weak signal. Basements, rural sites and steel-framed buildings all make uploading a job report harder than it should be.

What actually matters in a spec

A screen you can read in the van and in the sun. Brightness matters more than resolution here. The A8 is rated at 1000 nits, which is comfortably readable outdoors.

Battery and in-vehicle charging. A big battery plus a way to charge on the move means the device is full at every job.

Sealing and drop testing. IP67 or IP68 sealing covers the dust and water that come with the job, and a listed drop height or MIL-STD-810H rating tells you a device has been tested for falls. Check which ratings each device actually lists. Our IP68 vs IP67 guide explains the difference between the two sealing grades.

Your software decides the operating system. Most job management apps run on Android or in a browser. Some diagnostic and commissioning tools are Windows only, and if yours is, that settles it. Otherwise Android costs noticeably less for the same job.

We go into this in more depth in the best tablets for field engineers.

What we would pick

For most field service engineers, the Tuga A8 at £379. It is sealed to IP67, has a 1000 nit sunlight readable screen and a removable 8000mAh battery, so a charged spare covers the last job of the day. Dual SIM 4G helps where one network is weak, NFC is built in, and VESA mount points and pogo pin contacts let it lock into the Vehicle Mounting Dock. It works as a dashboard unit on the road and a job tablet on site. Two caveats: it lists no drop or MIL-STD rating, and it runs Android 12, older than the A6 and A10, so check your job management app supports it.

If you do not need a tablet-sized screen, the Tuga A6 at £349 is cheaper and goes in a pocket. It is sealed to IP67 and rated for 1.5 metre drops, has 4G, NFC and a removable 5050mAh battery, and the 13MP rear camera has a flash for dark ceiling voids and the back of plant. The built-in 2D barcode scanner reads parts labels and asset tags without a separate scanner. For engineers whose job sheets are short and whose main tasks are photos, scanning and sign-off, it is often all you need.

If your diagnostic or commissioning software only runs on Windows, the Tuga W8 at £629 is the one we would look at. It runs full Windows 11 Pro on an Intel Celeron N5100 with 8GB of RAM, has USB-C, USB-A and HDMI so you can plug into equipment directly, and a 700 nit screen. It is sealed to IP67 and tested to MIL-STD-810G. A version with a 2D barcode scanner is £699 if you scan parts or asset tags.

Accessories worth adding

For a van-based engineer, the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) is the most useful add-on: it locks the tablet in place and keeps it charged while you drive. If that is more than you need, a 12V DC Car Charger (£26) does the charging part. A Capacitive Stylus (£14.99) makes customer signatures legible, and the USB-C to USB-A OTG Adapter (£8) lets you plug in a USB drive or peripheral. For the A6, a Car Phone Mount (£17) and a Belt Holster (£22). Everything is on the accessories page.

Questions engineers ask

Can it replace my laptop?

For job sheets, manuals and reports, usually yes. For Windows-only diagnostic software, only the Windows models will do it.

Will it work as a sat nav in the van?

The A8 has GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou, and with the Vehicle Mounting Dock it sits on the dashboard and charges as you drive. Check your navigation app runs on its Android 12.

We have a fleet of engineers. Is there a discount?

Yes, automatically: 3% at 2 devices, 5% at 3 to 4, 8% at 5 to 9, 10% at 10 or more. Mix any models. See bulk pricing, or get in touch if you want to talk it through.

What happens if one breaks?

There is a 12-month warranty and UK email support on every device. For longer cover, the 3-Year Warranty is £65 to £89 per device, and business fleets of five or more devices on any model can ask for a Total Care quote, with a pre-imaged swap unit dispatched the same working day for claims accepted by 14:00.
